newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton settles firmer but off highs.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton settles firmer but off highs.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed firmer, having climbed to two-week highs during the session amid expectations for several pieces of bullish data, dealers said.
The most-active July contract ended 0.67 cent higher at 72.65 cents per lb, having ranged from 72.00 to 73.35 cents, its highest level since hitting 73.75 cents on April 30.
New-crop December finished 0.35 firmer at 74.67 cents.
Volume was estimated at 16,000 lots compared with Friday's official 8,983 lots.

Expectations for a decline in the net speculative short position in Tuesday's spec/hedge report, coupled with ongoing planting delays that should show up in today's planting progress report, lent support to the market.
While analysts initially viewed today's U.S. Department of Agriculture report as neutral, they said it may have helped to fuel the rally by indicating some tightness in world supplies.
The USDA raised U.S. ending stocks to 4.25 million bales from 4.05 million bales this season, and lowered world stocks by 1 million bales, to 36.54 million bales in 1997/98.
World consumption, meanwhile, rose to 88.5 million bales, from 86.44 million bales this year.
The higher use estimate contributed to the decline in stocks.
In the U.S., production was estimated at 18.50 million 480-lb bales, exports at 7.3 million bales, and domestic use at 11.0 million bales.
The USDA's final estimates for 1996/97 put output at 18.9 million bales, the third largest crop on record. Yields averaged 707 lbs per harvested acre, the second highest yield on record, USDA said.
